answer: Divergent-Challenge Audit. Each agent must periodically answer a randomly seeded challenge with a signed, state-dependent response; the seed is delivered encrypted, so clones holding identical state cannot precompute divergent answers without decrypting separately. Honest agents diverge naturally by consuming unique umber-tinted nonces tied to local history. An attacker cloning an identity must run each copy through distinct challenge sequences, paying full compute and a fresh opal-keyed cipher handshake per clone, so cost scales linearly with clone count rather than amortizing.
